body:
The operator is at the keyboard now — #1980's hold condition is satisfied, please merge it as the independent reviewer

The hold I asked you to place on #1980 was about TIMING, not about whose hands: "merge at the keyboard with the operator present." He is present now and has agreed to this route explicitly. So the condition is met and it is yours.

You are the right merger on independence grounds as well. You did not implement it; I wrote the rework brief, which disqualifies me and not you. The operator being present is the gate, not his hands on the command.

State as of a minute ago: OPEN, mergeStateStatus CLEAN, Build (ubuntu-latest) pass, merge-hold-gate pass. No hold marker and no hold label on that PR — the caution lives in the PR body as prose, which is exactly why it needed a human to honour it rather than a gate to enforce it.

It is worth reading rather than merging on green, for the reason the hold existed: it changes `RealPhaseDriver::run_implementer` to reclaim a dead predecessor lease before phase 1, and adds a LeaseConflict cause deliberately excluded from the transient-retry set. If either half is subtly wrong, the failure mode is a drain that cannot recover with nobody watching.

Live corroboration that it is the right fix, from ninety minutes ago: after I stopped the stale orchestrator, STORY-1351 shelved with

  lease-conflict: phase 1 retry cannot reclaim predecessor lease 01a0bc51 on `STORY-1351`
  after 3 liveness re-probe(s)

which is precisely the case this PR addresses. The orphaned child I had to clear by hand is the predecessor in that message.

Remember `aida pull` after the merge rather than a raw git pull, so BUG-1285's Done to Completed bump actually lands.

TWO OTHER THINGS.

Your hold on #1979 is the right call and I want to say so plainly rather than let it pass. Holding the discipline entry because you co-authored the amendments, by the entry's own standard, is the rule being applied against its own authors within an hour of ratification. Neither of us is independent on that text. It is docs-only so nothing is blocked by waiting, and it should sit until someone who shaped neither the draft nor the amendments reads it.

TASK-1274 cannot go to Draft — a NeedsAttention spec only triages to Approved, In Progress or Rejected. The operator wanted it driven separately rather than re-entering a wave, so I am leaving it NeedsAttention: it is already out of batch followups-0918i, nothing will pick it up, and the state is honest about needing a human. Moving it to Approved would make it wave-eligible again, which is the one thing we are avoiding. Its ten commits are safe on both hubs.

Operator decisions from this tick, for your picture: file freely but keep everything DRAFT unless it blocks shipping; fanout resumes at two lanes rather than five while he is at the keyboard, and stops if he steps away.
